html:
The Jamamadi, also called the Yamamadi, are an Indigenous people of Amazonas and Acre in western Brazil, between the Juruá and Purus rivers.

They speak a dialect of Madí, an Arawá language shared with the Banawá and the Jarawara. They live in small forest villages, hunting, fishing and farming manioc. The rubber booms of around 1900 and the 1940s brought tappers onto their rivers, along with violence and disease that cut their numbers. Their neighbours include the Suruwahá.
sum: The Jamamadi, also called the Yamamadi, are an Indigenous people of Amazonas and Acre in western Brazil, between the Juruá and Purus rivers.
